title: Musical Composition & Cultural Milestones: Megzenésít, megalkot, szimbólumává válik

sections.title: Connecting European and Hungarian Music History
sections.content: In Hungarian cultural discourse, musical achievements are expressed through creation verbs (*megzenésít* 'sets a poem to music', *megteremt* 'creates/founds') and the translative case (`-vá/-vé válik` 'becomes the symbol/foundation of').

sections.title: Official Exam Roster: European & Hungarian Composers (Explained)
rows: German Baroque master: his organ fugues, Brandenburg Concertos, and St Matthew Passion (Máté-passió) represent the pinnacle of Baroque polyphony and Christian sacred music.
Prodigy of Viennese Classicism (bécsi klasszicizmus): his operas The Magic Flute (A varázsfuvola) and Don Giovanni and his symphonies unite effortless melody with dramatic perfection.
Bridge from Classicism to Romanticism: composing even after losing his hearing, he set Schiller's Ode to Joy (Örömóda) in his Ninth Symphony — today the official anthem of the European Union.
Founder of Hungarian national opera (Hunyadi László, Bánk bán — featuring the patriotic aria 'Hazám, hazám') and composer of the music for Kölcsey's Himnusz in 1844.
Liszt Ferenc, Bartók Béla és Kodály Zoltán

Liszt brought Hungarian Rhapsodies to European concert halls and founded the Zeneakadémia (1875); Bartók and Kodály collected authentic peasant folksongs to renew 20th-century music and music education.

items.english: The final movement of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony, the Ode to Joy, became the official anthem of the European Union.

items.english: Ferenc Erkel set Ferenc Kölcsey's poem Himnusz to music in 1844.

items.spanish: Mozart és Beethoven a bécsi klasszicizmus legkiemelkedőbb zeneszerzői voltak.
items.english: Mozart and Beethoven were the most prominent composers of Viennese Classicism.
